name: Combs Intermediate School
district_operator: Ferguson-Florissant R-II School District (Florissant School District before the 1952 reorganization)
notes: Seed's 1876 opening is plausible: the Missouri Historical Society genealogy index (from Gretchen Crank's 'Reflections of the Florissant Valley', 1990) lists a 'St. Ferdinand Public School' at Washington St. between St. Jacques and St. Jean — the same block as today's Combs at 300 Rue St. Jean — and a district-history summary states the Florissant School District formed in 1871 and built St. Ferdinand Public School in 1876 (repeated on Grokipedia, an AI source, so year kept at 'probable'). The school's own website does not carry a founding year. Combs is 'famous for cherished artifact, the old St. Ferdinand School bell' (nomoz.org school listing), supporting the site lineage. The village public school was staffed by the Sisters of Loretto from the mid-1850s until 1887, when the public school board declined to license them (Florissant Valley Quarterly, July 2024). The origin of the 'Combs' name and when it was adopted were not found. School still operates as Combs Intermediate (grades 3-5).

name: Cross Keys School
district_operator: Florissant-area public school district (predecessor of Ferguson-Florissant R-II, exact district unverified)
notes: Real school, thinly documented online. The Missouri Historical Society genealogy index (from 'Reflections of the Florissant Valley', 1990) places 'Cross Keys School' on New Halls Ferry Road just north of Parker Road — in the old Cross Keys hamlet (which also had a general store and a post office per TownTapestry's Florissant history). The Florissant Valley Quarterly (Oct. 2022) prints a photo captioned 'Don Zykan Sr. in the 8th Grade class at Cross Keys School, Ferguson, 1942', confirming operation at least into 1942. Seed's 'Before 1951' opening and '1950s?' closing could not be verified; the 1950s hint is consistent with the 1952 Ferguson-Florissant R-II consolidation, but no source was found saying when the school closed or what absorbed it. A modern 'Cross Keys Middle School' (14205 Cougar Dr, Florissant 63033, still open) carries the community name but is a different institution — successor left 'unknown' rather than asserting continuity. Recommended human follow-up: Florissant Valley Historical Society files or FFSD records could pin down dates.

name: DeSmet School
notes: PARTIALLY UNVERIFIED: seed says 'Known Ferguson-Florissant school built in 1953' and an aggregated district history (Grokipedia, an AI-generated source that cites a district history) states 'DeSmet Elementary School opened in 1953 as the first new facility post-merger.' However, no independent confirmation was found: no 'DeSmet' school appears on current or recent FFSD rosters (2023-24 and 2026-27 district directories), on Wikipedia's list of former FFSD schools, or in the Missouri Historical Society's index of historic Florissant-area schools ('Reflections of the Florissant Valley'). Searches surface only De Smet Jesuit High School in Creve Coeur (unrelated, est. 1967) and DeSmet Public School in Missoula, MT. The school presumably existed (name honors Fr. Pierre DeSmet, ordained at St. Ferdinand in 1827) but has likely been renamed or closed — candidate renames could not be established. Recommend human follow-up: FFSD records center or Florissant Valley Historical Society should confirm the school, its address, and its fate before Track B spends effort on it.

name: Sacred Heart Catholic School
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: the parish's own history page states the first building constructed was the school — a two-story brick building at the corner of Jefferson and St. Louis Streets, opened September 1866; the upper floor served as the convent. Corroborated by the State Historical Society of Missouri finding aid for the Sacred Heart Church of Florissant records (S0052): 'Jesuits established Sacred Heart in 1866... that year, the first combination school and convent opened.' Sisters of St. Joseph taught first, joined/replaced by Sisters of the Most Precious Blood in 1877, who served until 1994. A second two-story classroom/teacherage was added in 1872 (not a separate seed row). The parish school remains open as Sacred Heart Catholic School at 501 St. Louis St (school site live, PK-8), independent of the 2018 All Saints Academy partnership. Building-level lineage is split across ALL-006/007/008. NOTE: the school website (shcs-flo.org/history) prints 'September 15, 1886' for the first day of school — internally inconsistent with its own 'twenty years later in 1866' framing and with the parish history and SHSMO; treated as a typo for 1866.

name: Sacred Heart School - 1866 Building
historical_names: Sacred Heart combination school and convent
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: First school building of the Sacred Heart parish school lineage (see ALL-005): two-story brick at Jefferson & St. Louis Sts, opened September 1866 with classrooms below and convent above. When the new school at St. Denis & Jefferson was dedicated November 28, 1889, this building 'remained as a convent for the Sisters' — it ceased school use in 1889 and the convent portion burned in 1903 (replaced 1904 by the convent building still standing at St. Louis & Jefferson). Successor recorded as the 1889 building (ALL-007), which took over classes.

name: Sacred Heart School - 1889 Building
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: replacement school at the corner of St. Denis and Jefferson Streets, plans drawn fall 1888, 'solemnly dedicated by the Very Rev. Henry Muehlsiepen, Vicar General of St. Louis, on Thanksgiving Day, November 28, 1889' (parish and school history pages). Upper-grade classes moved to the new St. Louis Street building in 1952 — the basis for 'closed 1952' — but the building did not stop being used for education: the school's own history says it is 'today home for Preschool and Kindergarten students' and 'was also used by the Archdiocesan Special Education Learning Center for over 30 years.' Closed_year kept at 1952 (probable) meaning 'ceased to be the main school,' with the continued PreK/K use noted here.

name: Sacred Heart School - 1952 Building
district_operator: Sacred Heart Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: 'In 1952 it became necessary to build a new school. The corner stone was laid on March 23, 1952. It faced St. Louis Street' (parish history); the school opened for the 1952-53 year per the seed and remains the operating Sacred Heart Catholic School at 501 St. Louis St. Still open (school website active; independent of All Saints Academy).

name: St. Ferdinand School
district_operator: St. Ferdinand Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Resolved seed's 'Unknown' opening: the parish school of St. Ferdinand's dates from 1887 — Gilbert Garraghan's 1923 history (Jesuit Archives, chap. 42) states the parish school 'dates from 1887' and opened September 1887 in temporary quarters in the Sisters' house, and the Florissant Valley Quarterly (July 2024) gives the exact opening as September 5, 1887 after the public school board declined to license the Sisters of Loretto. A permanent parochial schoolhouse at Old St. Ferdinand was built in 1888 (May 1888 bid letter). Older school tradition on the site: St. Rose Philippine Duchesne's girls' school (1819) and the Loretto-staffed village public school (from the 1840s/mid-1850s until 1887) — related institutions, not the parochial school itself. The school moved to the current Charbonier Road campus in 1955 (parish history: first Mass 1955 in the 'combination church and school building'; additions through the 1960s). In 2018 the school merged into the All Saints Academy partnership and its campus became All Saints Academy - St. Ferdinand Campus (ALL-014); recorded closed 2018 as an independent school. St. Sabina and St. Martin de Porres parishes were merged into St. Ferdinand Parish in 2023 (post-dates the school merger).

name: St. Sabina School
district_operator: St. Sabina Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed verbatim by the (now-merged) parish's surviving history page: 'St. Sabina Parish was founded in 1960... St. Sabina School opened in 1961 and closed in 2010. The parish was merged into St. Ferdinand Parish in 2023.' The church at 1625 Swallow Lane was built as 'a gymnasium attached to a school' and dedicated in 1963 (April 2026 canonical closure decree, St. Louis Review). NUANCE: after the parish school closed, the site hosted 'The Academy at St. Sabina' — an Archdiocese of St. Louis Department of Special Education school for students with special needs (~29-30 students, NCES PSS 2015-16 and 2017-18; still open as of January 2019 per flovalleynews.com). It closed within 2016-2021 per the Feb. 2021 St. Louis Review article on Trinity Catholic. The Academy was a different institution (special-education program), so no successor school_id is recorded; the site detail is noted for whoever surveys yearbooks there.

name: St. Norbert School
district_operator: St. Norbert Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed by the parish's own history pages: St. Norbert School opened September 1988 with grades K-3 (first principal Sr. Rosalie Wisneski, OSF), added a grade each year, and graduated its first class in 1995. In August 2018 it became part of the All Saints Academy partnership school — its campus is now All Saints Academy - St. Norbert Campus (ALL-013). Parish itself was founded May 18, 1965 (Cardinal Ritter); church first Mass Sept. 3, 1967. MINOR FLAG: seed and the parish use 16455 New Halls Ferry Road; the academy's admissions page prints '16475 New Halls Ferry Rd' — likely a typo on the academy site.

name: All Saints Academy - St. Norbert Campus
district_operator: All Saints Academy (partnership of St. Norbert, St. Ferdinand and formerly St. Rose Philippine Duchesne parishes) / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: All Saints Academy was announced January 25, 2018 and opened for the 2018-19 school year as a partnership-model school uniting St. Ferdinand, St. Norbert and St. Rose Philippine Duchesne schools (St. Louis Review, Feb. 2018 and Aug. 2018). The St. Norbert campus continues at the former St. Norbert School site on New Halls Ferry Rd. Still operating — the academy's admissions site lists St. Ferdinand and St. Norbert campuses; the third campus (St. Rose Philippine Duchesne) closed after the 2022-23 year amid enrollment decline (St. Louis Review, June 2023).

name: All Saints Academy - St. Ferdinand Campus
district_operator: All Saints Academy (partnership of St. Ferdinand, St. Norbert and formerly St. Rose Philippine Duchesne parishes) / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Seed confirmed: this is the St. Ferdinand School campus operating under the All Saints Academy partnership since the 2018-19 school year (successor entity to ALL-009). Still operating at 1735 Charbonier Rd (~180 students per the St. Ferdinand parish history page). The third ASA campus, St. Rose Philippine Duchesne, closed in 2023, leaving St. Ferdinand and St. Norbert as the two remaining campuses.

name: North County Christian School
district_operator: Private (founded by Ferguson Church of the Nazarene)
notes: SEED ERROR: seed lists opened 1994; the school was actually founded in 1962 as 'North County Day School' by Rev. Udell G. Moss, starting as a kindergarten in the Ferguson Church of the Nazarene basement (one teacher, twelve students). Confirmed by the school's history as republished by the Greater North County Chamber and by a 2012 Florissant Patch article marking its 50th anniversary. It moved to 1309 N. Elizabeth in Ferguson in 1966, then purchased the current 14-acre campus at 845 Dunn Road, Florissant on July 8, 2004 — grades 1-12 moved in within 50 days, preschool/kindergarten followed August 2005, remaining fields acquired 2007. privateschoolreview lists 'Year Founded 1962'. Still operating (PK-12). The seed's 1994 is unexplained — possibly a conflation with a re-incorporation or expansion year.

name: Atonement Lutheran School
notes: Seed's 'Unknown' opening resolved to 1956 (probable): privateschoolreview states 'Established in 1956, Atonement Lutheran School is a non-profit parochial school in Florissant, MO operated by the Lutheran Church of the Atonement.' The congregation itself was founded in 1951 per St. Louis Patina's profile of the church building — consistent with a 1956 school start. Still operating (PK-8, ~220 students per elementaryschools.org; school site alcs-web.com active). SEED ERROR: district/operator listed as 'LCMS' — the school is ELCA (the comparison profile explicitly says 'E.L.C.A.', and the congregation's materials use ELCA branding). One source (MoHistory index, 'Reflections of the Florissant Valley') maps a 'Lutheran Church of the Atonement' at St. Francois at St. Ferdinand St. — an earlier church site; the school/church sit on N. New Florissant Rd today.

name: Grace Christian Academy
district_operator: Private Christian (ministry of Dorsett Village Church since 2012)
notes: Seed's 'Unknown' opening resolved: the school's own history page (fcastl.org) says 'On August 31st, 1981, the doors of Grace Christian School were opened for the very first time' with 96 students. Same address and phone as the NCES 'Grace Christian Academy' listing (2890 Patterson Rd, 314-837-8283; PSS 2023-24, K-8, 54 students) — the school now brands itself 'Foundation Christian Academy' and the legal nonprofit is 'Grace Christian Academy St Louis' (EIN 83-4588278, 501(c)(3) ruling March 2023). Itinerary: opened 1981 → purchased Penn Junction Elementary from Pattonville SD in May 1985 (home for 28 years) → became a ministry of Dorsett Village Church January 2012 → ~4 years in the Briarcrest building (Pattonville) → ~1 year in Overland → moved in 2018 into the Christ First Church facility at 2890 Patterson Rd, Florissant. So the school only arrived at the seed's address in 2018; pre-2018 attendance records would live under earlier names/addresses. Still operating.
